stories.title: Burnham sets UK–EU summit for 20 November
stories.summary: The PM called for serious dialogue about the longer-term relationship, while prioritising food, youth-mobility and emissions-trading deals. These are negotiations and ambitions, not completed agreements.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🤖 Tech / AI / Digital — government outlines AI cyber-security measures
stories.summary: Measures include extending AI vulnerability-detection pilots, examining targeted changes to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, and learning from near misses. This is policy and programme development, not an announced supplier contract.

stories.title: 💰 Spending / VfM — IFS warns of £35bn Budget challenge
stories.summary: The IFS says Chancellor John Healey needs a substantial top-up to meet defence and health ambitions without squeezing other departments. This is a think-tank assessment ahead of the 28 October Budget, not an announced spending cut or funding settlement.

stories.title: 🏢 Vendor signal — Accenture and Dell launch private-AI business group
stories.summary: The alliance targets private, sovereign and specialist GPU-cloud infrastructure; Accenture plans to train more than 3,000 practitioners. TechMarketView names RHAELM as a client but reports no investment figure or revenue target; this is not evidence of a UK government award.

stories.title: Badenoch challenges PM's Brexit-interference language
stories.summary: The Conservative leader criticised Burnham's statements about Russia and the referendum. No. 10 said he accepts the result as legitimate; his allegation of attempted interference is not evidence that Russia changed the outcome.

topics.name: Liberal Democrats
topics.description: Lib Dem party news, policy positions

stories.title: Opinion: Guardian argues against replacing Ed Davey
stories.summary: The editorial discusses pressure on Davey's leadership ahead of a Tuesday meeting and argues his seat-focused strategy should continue. This is attributed commentary, not confirmation that a confidence vote has been triggered.

topics.name: Reform UK
topics.description: Nigel Farage, Reform UK party news

stories.title: Reform proposes five-year asylum freeze and immediate deportations
stories.summary: Farage's plan includes about 90,000 pending asylum cases and would not exempt children or mothers. Refugee charities called the proposals unworkable; these are opposition proposals, not current UK policy.

stories.title: Farage says he would scrutinise Britain's Ukraine support
stories.summary: Farage said a Reform government would examine whether UK aid is being lost to corruption, while saying support should continue and acknowledging Putin's threat. His corruption allegations are attributed claims, not established findings about British aid.

stories.title: No investigation into Swinney's pension remarks
stories.summary: Independent advisers decided no investigation was required after Swinney referred himself over claims he misled Holyrood about pension changes. Scottish Conservative leader Russell Findlay continued to demand a correction.

stories.title: Polling transparency: Farage adviser's role at Redfield & Wilton
stories.summary: The Guardian reports Chris Bruni-Lowe had an influential, unpublicised role at the polling firm. Its director acknowledged consultancy work but denied an institutional or financial relationship with Farage or Reform; this is a transparency story, not a new election result or poll.
